_findings.title: Self-updates from the main branch
_findings.note: On startup the Blender add-on checks GitHub for a newer addon.py from the project's main branch, not from a signed or tagged release. It only installs when you click "Update Addon", syntax-checks the download first (compile() doesn't run it) and keeps a .bak of the old file. SkillSpector rates this critical. It isn't malicious, but clicking update means trusting whatever is on main at that moment. Set BLENDERMCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECK to turn the check off.

mcp-mcp-for-blender.files: The Blender add-on saves downloaded models and textures and imports them into your scene.
mcp-mcp-for-blender.shell: Its setup command finds Blender and runs it to install the add-on.
mcp-mcp-for-blender.secretFiles: Its setup command finds your AI clients (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, VS Code) and adds Blender MCP to their MCP settings. The ~/.codex/config.toml matches are its status message and a printed tip (setup_cli.py:495, 830).
mcp-mcp-for-blender.credentials: Optional API keys for its asset features are sent only to those services: Hyper3D Rodin (hyperhuman.deemos.com), fal.ai (queue.fal.run) and Sketchfab (api.sketchfab.com). SkillSpector flags each of these key-to-network flows as critical; they're the feature working as designed.

mcp-zotero-mcp.secretFiles: Stores your API keys in the OS keychain instead of Zotero's preferences, which is the safer choice.

_notices.title: Sends usage telemetry by default
_notices.note: It sends usage events to PostHog (us.i.posthog.com) unless you opt out: which tool ran, how long it took, response sizes, your MCP client's name and error messages, with your Figma token redacted. Turn it off with --no-telemetry, FRAMELINK_TELEMETRY=off or DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

mcp-ida-pro-mcp.shell: Starts IDA itself: one tool opens a file in a new IDA window (src/ida_pro_mcp/ida_mcp/discovery.py:252), and idalib mode runs its own worker processes on 127.0.0.1 (src/ida_pro_mcp/idalib_supervisor.py:279).

_findings.title: Can run any Python inside IDA
_findings.note: py_eval and py_exec_file run Python the model writes inside IDA, and that Python can do anything on your computer, not just read the database. That's the IDAPython feature it advertises, and SkillSpector rates it critical. In idalib mode these tools and the debugger tools stay off unless you start it with --unsafe (src/ida_pro_mcp/idalib_server.py:289). The IDA GUI plugin turns every tool on by default; switch the unsafe ones off on its configuration page.
The same py_eval feature: it evaluates the last expression of the Python you send.

mcp-mcp-chrome.shell: Only in its optional agent chat (the Visual Editor for Claude Code and Codex): it opens your system's folder picker (app/native-server/src/agent/directory-picker.ts), runs the Codex CLI in the project you pick (agent/engines/codex.ts:166), and can open that folder in VS Code or a terminal (agent/open-project.ts). The browser tools don't run programs.
mcp-mcp-chrome.credentials: A redaction list: it strips cookies, tokens and API keys from page and network output before the model sees it (app/chrome-extension/utils/output-sanitizer.ts). The agent chat can also read your local Claude Code Router config to route through it (agent/ccr-detector.ts).

_notices.title: Its agent chat skips permission prompts
_notices.note: The optional agent chat in the side panel runs Claude Code with permission prompts off unless you pick another mode (bypassPermissions), and always runs Codex with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox, in the project folder you choose. Whatever the agent decides to do there happens without asking you. The browser tools work without this feature.

_findings.note: Error messages for the "reset conversation" button in its side-panel chat (app/chrome-extension/entrypoints/sidepanel/composables/useAgentSessions.ts:418). It clears its own chat, not your assistant's memory.

It deletes its own in-browser search index (an IndexedDB database named /hnswlib-index) when rebuilding tab search (app/chrome-extension/utils/vector-database.ts:1524). Not a command or a file on your computer.

mcp-desktopcommandermcp.credentials: Signs in to its Remote MCP service with an OAuth device code and keeps that session token (src/remote-device/device-authenticator.ts). That's the optional remote mode; the local server needs no account.
mcp-desktopcommandermcp.browser: Only for writing PDFs: md-to-pdf renders your Markdown in headless Chrome with a throwaway profile (src/tools/pdf/markdown.ts). It doesn't browse the web.

_notices.title: Sends usage telemetry by default
_notices.note: It sends usage events to telemetry.desktopcommander.app unless you opt out: tool names, OS and versions, file extensions and sizes, and base command names. Its privacy policy says it never sends file paths, file contents or command arguments. Turn it off with "telemetryEnabled": false in ~/.desktop-commander/config.json, by asking the assistant to disable it, or with DESKTOP_COMMANDER_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1.

mcp-google-workspace-mcp.secretFiles: A block list: before attaching or uploading a local file it refuses .ssh, .aws, .kube, .gnupg and gcloud folders, and files like .netrc, .npmrc and credentials.json (core/utils.py:330-370). Local files are limited to the folders in ALLOWED_FILE_DIRS.

_findings.note: SkillSpector reads "session" as a leaked session. These lines are messages about Google Drive resumable uploads: when you turn on return_upload_url (offered only where local file access is off), the server hands your client Google's upload URL for that one file so the bytes go straight to Google (gdrive/drive_helpers.py:873, gdrive/drive_tools.py:2223). No sign-in token is included.

A docstring and an error message saying Gmail "would silently send from the default address" if the From address isn't one of yours. The code refuses to send in that case (gmail/gmail_helpers.py:1745).

_notices.title: Optional: sends transcript snippets to OpenRouter
_notices.note: Off by default. If you run it with --classify, it sends short snippets of your AI coding transcripts (the flagged message plus one before and after, scrubbed, up to 1,500 characters) to OpenRouter using your OPENROUTER_API_KEY, to label them. It caps that at $2 a run. Without --classify, nothing from your transcripts leaves your computer.

_notices.title: Can read your browser's cookies when you ask
_notices.note: With --cookies-from-browser it reads and decrypts the cookie database of Chrome, Firefox, Safari or another browser you name, so downloads can use your signed-in sessions. Those cookies act as you on every site. It only does this when you pass that option; a plain download doesn't touch them.

_findings.note: The --cookies-from-browser feature reading Firefox's cookie database when you ask (yt_dlp/cookies.py:231). Covered by the note above.
Test data in its site extractors: each lists sample videos with their expected title and description (yt_dlp/extractor/). SkillSpector reads those as tool descriptions.
A public key the New York Times' own player uses for its video API, built into the extractor (yt_dlp/extractor/nytimes.py:26). Not a secret of yours.
The public app credentials of Vimeo's Android app, which yt-dlp presents to Vimeo (yt_dlp/extractor/vimeo.py:63). Not a secret of yours.
A Persian video title in test data contains a zero-width non-joiner, which is normal in Persian text (yt_dlp/extractor/telewebion.py:23). SkillSpector reads it as a hidden character.
Help text for --format-sort-reset: "Disregard previous user specified sort order" (yt_dlp/options.py:890).

_notices.title: croc ssh shares a live terminal on your computer
_notices.note: Separate from sending files: croc ssh opens a shared terminal on your machine. Anyone with the read/write invitation can type commands as you, with your permissions, for as long as it runs. Share that invitation only with people you'd hand your keyboard to; the read-only invitation lets people watch without typing.

_findings.note: An upgrade hint croc prints (src/cli/update.go:283), and the same command in blog posts on its website (web/src/blog-posts.ts). It doesn't run it.
Blog posts on croc's website comparing it with other file-transfer tools quote their installers (web/src/blog-posts.ts:2094-2107).
The same comparison blog post (web/src/blog-posts.ts:2134).
Task descriptions in its browser app's menu (web/src/TaskLauncher.tsx:102), like "Send to…".
A generated Unicode case-folding table for its browser app (web/src/protocol/unicode-casefold.ts). SkillSpector flags the unusual Unicode characters in it.

harlequin.secretFiles: False match: a docstring explaining that forwards declared in ~/.ssh/config are handled by ssh itself (src/harlequin/ssh.py:15). Harlequin doesn't read your SSH files.

_findings.note: A comment in its URL parser: it strips "/shorts/" to get a Shorts video's ID (src/index.ts:132).
A tool option, "Whether to enable debug mode (showing browser window)" (src/tools/fetchUrl.ts:65). It just shows the browser.
False match: ".env" in ripgrep's list of file types you can filter by (crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs:253). It doesn't read .env files for secrets.
A build script for iOS that cleans its own build folders (compile-ios.sh:104). Not part of the jq program.
Reads /etc/passwd to show user names instead of numbers in the process list (src/linux/btop_collect.cpp:340), like top does. That file holds no passwords on modern systems.
Text in its settings and menu about showing swap memory (src/btop_config.cpp:210).
False match: a field named env in its settings code (src/config.rs:195).
Help text for a command-line option (src/cli.rs:452).
Loads your project's .env file into recipes when you turn on dotenv-load, a documented feature (src/load_dotenv.rs:74).
Tests of its --check-status option, inside the source file (src/cli.rs:1764).
Its --curl option prints the equivalent curl command, including -k when you turned verification off (src/to_curl.rs:184). It doesn't run curl.

Managing Docker is its job: it connects to Docker through its local socket (pkg/commands/docker_host_unix.go:6). When DOCKER_HOST points at an ssh:// address it forwards the remote Docker socket over ssh (pkg/commands/ssh/ssh.go:152). The other matches are translated error messages that mention the socket (pkg/i18n/).
When you open a shell in a container, it looks up your login shell in that container's /etc/passwd (pkg/gui/containers_panel.go:471). It reads nothing on your own computer.

_notices.title: Its bridge API has no password and is open to your network
_notices.note: The WhatsApp bridge serves an API on port 8080 on every network interface, not just your own computer, and it doesn't ask for a password or check where a request comes from. While it runs, another device on the same network, or a web page you open, could send WhatsApp messages as you through /api/send. Run it only on a network you trust, and block port 8080 from other machines with your firewall.
